title: How Shopify Orchestrates AI-Powered Mobile App Development Without Overloading Developers' Machines
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/shopify-remote-ai-dev/en/headerimage/shopify-ruvy-ruby-wasm-1794947458635.jpeg"/><p>To prevent AI development workflows from exhausting developer machines' resources, Shopify built Remote Dev, a remote mobile development environment that enables AI agents to independently build, test and maintain iOS and Android applications and in parallel.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Qwik 2.0 RC: Replaces HTML Comment Markers for Faster Reactivity and Out-of-Order Streaming
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/quik-2-streaming/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794907611481.jpg"/><p>Qwik 2.0 Release Candidate, published on 1 October 2026, replaces v1's HTML comment markers with two script blocks that hold state and virtual node data. It adds experimental out-of-order streaming, async useComputed$, and cacheable route loaders. Qwik's benchmarks show v2 at 1.23x vanilla JavaScript, versus 2.59x for v1. A migration command is provided.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Datadog Brings Production Experimentation to AI Agent Observability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/datadog-ai-agent-observability/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794408423767.jpg"/><p>Datadog is extending its Agent Observability platform with Online Experiments, allowing engineering teams to compare AI agent versions against real production traffic rather than relying exclusively on predefined evaluation datasets.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Microsoft Releases .NET 11: C# 15 Union Types, Native AOT CLI Host, and CoreCLR by Default in MAUI
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Microsoft has released .NET 11, a Standard Term Support release with two years of support. It ships C# 15 with union types and closed hierarchies, a Native AOT CLI host, a preview of Runtime Async, Zstandard compression, asynchronous validation and OpenAPI 3.2 in ASP.NET Core, CoreCLR as the default runtime in .NET MAUI, and EF Core 11 with experimental vector search.</p> <i>By Almir Vuk</i>

title: Production AI, Architecture Trade-offs & Team Design: InfoQ Opens Registration for 6 January Cohorts
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/onlinecohort-jan27-certification/en/headerimage/onlinecohorts-jan27-certifications-1794839939505.jpg"/><p>From agent reliability to architecture decisions and delivery bottlenecks, InfoQ’s January 2027 cohorts give senior practitioners five weeks to examine current challenges, test approaches in their own work, and compare results with peers.</p> <i>By Artenisa Chatziou</i>

title: Presentation: Scaling LLM-Based Ranking Systems for Latency-Critical Search & Recommendation Workloads
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/scale-llm-ranking-systems-linkedin/en/mediumimage/SundaraRamanRamachandran-medium-1793279019345.jpeg"/><p>Sundara Raman Ramachandran shares how LinkedIn productionizes LLM ranking under strict P99 latency SLAs. He discusses distilling a 7B model down to 400M parameters, compressing job contexts into single-token embeddings for a 10x throughput leap, and eliminating hidden system bottlenecks - from custom flash attention masks to Python GIL workarounds, gc.freeze, and non-blocking CUDA memory copies.</p> <i>By Sundara Raman Ramachandran</i>

title: Ten Years On, Google Updates the SRE Book for the AI Era
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-sre-book-ai-era/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794674690062.jpg"/><p>Google has announced a completely rewritten second edition of Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems, ten years after the original book was published by O'Reilly Media. The update reframes SRE around modern cloud architectures, platform engineering and AI workloads, while retaining the discipline's original emphasis on applying software engineering to operations.</p> <i>By Matt Saunders</i>

title: Java News Roundup: Lazy Constants, Spring for Apache Pulsar, GlassFish, Hibernate, TomEE, Seed4J
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/java-news-roundup-nov09-2026/en/headerimage/java-news-roundup-image-1794842460564.jpg"/><p>This week's Java roundup for November 9th, 2026, features news highlighting: Lazy Constants proposed to target for JDK 28; TornadoVM jitLLM 3.0; point releases of Seed4J; second release candidates of Spring AI and Spring Boot; first release candidates of Hibernate ORM and Hibernate Reactive; fourth milestone release of GlassFish; and the second milestone release of Apache TomEE.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

title: Uber’s Legal AI Agent Cuts Contract Review Time by 20% with Rules and RAG
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Uber’s Legal Redlining Agent reviews contract changes in Microsoft Word using RAG, historical lawyer feedback, and deterministic policy rules. Built with LangGraph, OpenSearch, and Redis, the system reports more than 20% lower average contract review time and 91% accuracy in AI-generated decisions. Uber is exploring agentic harnesses, skills, legal ontologies, and knowledge graphs.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Airbnb Introduces CASTLE for Training Natural Language Search Models with Synthetic Data
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Airbnb researchers have introduced CASTLE, a framework designed to address the cold-start problem in natural language search. The approach uses de-identified booking sessions and large language models (LLMs) to jointly generate synthetic search queries and relevance labels, enabling model training before sufficient real search traffic is available.</p> <i>By Robert Krzaczyński</i>

title: Article: Governed Autonomous Intelligence for Mission-Critical Utility
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/utility-governed-autonomous-intelligence-ai/en/headerimage/utility-governed-autonomous-intelligence-ai-header-1793368487796.jpg"/><p>The article describes an architecture for agentic AI in regulated utility operations. Agents reason and propose actions, but a deterministic policy gate and a governed tool gateway control execution, with human approval where required. It covers an AWS reference implementation, grounding in runbooks, governed prediction, outcome validation, audit evidence, and phased autonomy.</p> <i>By Purnang Borah</i>

title: Podcast: Getting CRA Compliant Hardens the Code and Gets Your Company Closer to Digital Sovereignty
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/company-closer-digital-sovereignty/en/smallimage/infoq-podcast-500-1794318137932.jpg"/><p>In this episode, Christopher "CRob" Robinson, CTO of OpenSSF, Akrites and Chief Security Architect of the Linux Foundation, explores the state of software supply chain security amid multiple security incidents and explains how tools like Scorecard, the Security Baseline framework, and SLSA help harden software.</p> <i>By Christopher Robinson</i>

title: AWS Open-Sources Emulator for Local Testing of 200+ Services by Coding Agents
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-emulator-agents/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794516406278.jpg"/><p>AWS Emulator is a generally available local HTTPS endpoint, generated from public Smithy API models, that lets developers and coding agents test against more than 200 AWS services without an account, with published fidelity scores and documented limits around IAM, regions, and in-memory state.</p> <i>By Daniel Dominguez</i>

title: GitHub Rebuilds the Copilot App's Diff Surface to Open Million-Line Pull Requests Without Jank
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/github-pull-requests-rebuild/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794747791339.jpg"/><p>GitHub engineers rebuilt the diff view in the Copilot app to handle a pull request with 2,200 files, over a million changed lines and 400 inline comments. The design separates fixed-height code rows from variable-height comment blocks, which are measured in batches near the viewport. Performance is checked through CI budgets and automated app runs.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: AWS Nitro Sandboxes Put Each EKS Pod in Its Own MicroVM with One RuntimeClass Field
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/aws-nitro-sandboxes-eks/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794301940782.jpg"/><p>AWS has launched Nitro Sandboxes, running each opted-in EKS pod, ECS task or EC2 workload in its own Firecracker microVM with a separate kernel, enabled by one runtimeClassName field at no extra charge. A confidential mode adds attestation-gated key release. The documentation lists the trade-offs: no GPU passthrough, at most five sandboxes per vCPU, and half the compute on SMT instances.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>
